To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hyperglycemic conditions in diabetes augment cutaneous O2 levels, at least partly via the NADPH-oxidase and protein kinase-C pathways, resulting in delayed wound healing in type-1 diabetes.
hyperglycemic conditions increase cutaneous O2 levels via NADPH and protein kinase C, resulting in impaired healing in type 2 diabetic mice.
gene transfer of eNOS and MnSOD restores delayed wound healing in diabetic mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapies for the treatment of diabetic wounds.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the impaired wound healing in diabetes mellitus and the development of novel strategies to restore wound healing in diabetes.
the molecular basis and pathophysiological significance of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (e-NOS) and manganese superoxide dismitase (Mn-SOD) gene therapy in diabetic wound healing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that gene therapy of eNos or MnSOD can restore delayed wound healing in streptozocin induced type 1 diabetic mouse model.
gene therapy with eNOS and MnSOD can restore wound healing in diabetic mice, which is associated with a reduction in cutaneous O2 − and an increase in NO bioavailability.
hyperglycemic conditions in type 1 diabetics cause an increase in cutaneous superoxide levels via NADPH and protein kinase C (PKC) pathways, which results in impaired wound healing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hyperglycemia-induced oxidative stress contributes to diabetic wound-healing impairment.
we have shown that gene transfer of eNOS and/or MnSOD can improve diabetic wound healing.
we have shown that hyperglycemic conditions in diabetes cause an increase in superoxide levels, at least partially, via the protein kinase C pathway and NADPH oxidases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene therapy of eNOs and/or MnSOD can be used as a novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of delayed wound healing in type I diabetes.
the use of gene therapy strategies to restore cutaneous NO bioactivity may be an effective means to improve diabetic wound healing.
the use of gene transfer of eNOS and MnSOD can be a useful tool to treat diabetic foot ulcers.
